// multibody/contact_solvers/icf/icf_solver.cc:364
DRAKE_THROW_UNLESS(dell0 < 0, dell0);

new_candidates.body:
### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

Related but different issue I found:

- #4668 (closed): many dropped packets on 127.0.0.1 when many processes start at the same time. Those drops happen in the kernel. The datagrams in this issue are received by Fast DDS and then discarded by Fast DDS itself.

### Expected behavior

When a participant joins a domain where other participants are already running, it discovers them as soon as they answer its first `DATA(p)`. On localhost that takes a few milliseconds.

### Current behavior

Some remote participants are discovered only at their next periodic announcement, so 0 to 3 s later with the default `leaseDuration_announcementperiod`. Endpoint matching waits for that as well. The time until a new participant has matched all remote endpoints is therefore bimodal. Either everything matches within a few tens of milliseconds, or part of it takes 1 to 3 s.

Fast DDS logs nothing when this happens.

#### Root cause: the first announcement is sent before the receivers are registered

References are for `master` (3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007). v2.14.x has the same code.

1. **The reception threads run before any `MessageReceiver` is attached.**
   - `setup_meta_traffic()` and `setup_user_traffic()` call `createReceiverResources(..., RegisterReceiver = false, ...)` ([RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp:641-642](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp#L641-L642), [:706-707](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp#L706-L707)).
   - The UDP channel resource starts its listening thread in its constructor ([UDPChannelResource.cpp:50](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/transport/UDPChannelResource.cpp#L50)), so datagrams are read from the socket from that point on.
2. **Datagrams that arrive without a registered receiver are discarded.** [ReceiverResource.cpp:121-123](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/network/ReceiverResource.cpp#L121-L123): `if (rcv != nullptr && active_callbacks_ >= 0) { ... }` has no `else`.
3. **The first announcement is sent before the receivers are registered.**
   - [RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp:790-799](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp#L790-L799) calls `mp_builtinProtocols->enable()` first, and runs the `RegisterReceiver()` loop after it.
   - [BuiltinProtocols.cpp:157-165](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/BuiltinProtocols.cpp#L157-L165): `enable()` is `PDP::enable()` + `announceParticipantState(true)` + `resetParticipantAnnouncement()`.
   - The SPDP writer sends synchronously, so the first `DATA(p)` goes to every initial peer and multicast locator on the calling thread before `enable()` returns.
4. **A remote participant answers a new participant only once.**
   - On the first `DATA(p)` from an unknown participant, `PDPListener::process_alive_data()` creates the proxy and calls `assignRemoteEndpoints()`. Matching the remote SPDP reader marks the local `DATA(p)` as unsent, so it is sent to the newcomer right away. The comment at [PDPListener.cpp:211-221](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDPListener.cpp#L211-L221) describes this.
   - Every later `DATA(p)` from the same participant, including the initial announcements every 100 ms, takes the `update_data()` path ([PDPListener.cpp:229-244](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDPListener.cpp#L229-L244)). That path sends no answer.
5. **Recovery waits for the remote's periodic announcement** ([PDP.cpp:1502](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDP.cpp#L1502)). Until then the newcomer does not know the remote participant, so it also ignores the remote's EDP traffic.

On localhost an answer arrives within microseconds. With a few dozen participants, some answers routinely land between the first send and the `RegisterReceiver()` loop. The window grows with the number of destination locators, because the sends are synchronous, and with CPU contention.

#### Affected versions

- **Reproduced:**
  - the `ros-jazzy-fastrtps` 2.14.7 binary
  - v2.14.4 built from source (reproducer below)
  - `master` 3b496678 and the `2.14.x` head b904a742, with the regression test from https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/pull/6631
- **Same order in `RTPSParticipantImpl::enable()` by inspection:** v2.6.10, v2.10.6, v2.14.7, v3.0.2, v3.6.2.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained Docker reproducer: two small programs using the plain Fast DDS C++ API (no ROS 2), a run script and a Dockerfile. **https://gist.github.com/SeanChangX/4b77ef56d31f00fb1bddfda9e2eb827b**

1. 24 long-lived processes, each with one participant and one `DataReader` on `race_topic`.
2. Participant QoS:
   - builtin transports off, one `UDPv4TransportDescriptor` with `maxInitialPeersRange = 32`
   - `metatrafficMulticastLocatorList` cleared, metatraffic unicast UDPv4 "any"
   - `initialPeersList = { 127.0.0.1 }`
   - default discovery timings
3. A new participant with the same QoS and a `DataWriter` on `race_topic` is started 40 times in a row. Each time, the reproducer measures how long it takes until `PublicationMatchedStatus::current_count == 24`.

```sh
docker build -t fastdds-startup-race .
docker run --rm --network none -e RUNS=40 fastdds-startup-race /repro/run.sh /repro/build-stock
docker run --rm --network none -e RUNS=40 -e LOAD=16 fastdds-startup-race /repro/run.sh /repro/build-instr
```

The `build-instr` build adds an instrumentation patch. When `FASTDDS_LOG_DROPS` is set, it logs every datagram that `ReceiverResource::OnDataReceived()` discards because no receiver is registered.

Results on an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (22 logical CPUs), Ubuntu 24.04, Docker `--network none`. "Slow" means not all 24 readers matched within 1 s:

| Build | CPU load | Slow runs | Median / max time to match all 24 | Runs with `DATA(p)` dropped during `enable()` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ros-jazzy-fastrtps` 2.14.7 binary | idle | **16/40** | 125 / 3123 ms | (not instrumented) |
| `ros-jazzy-fastrtps` 2.14.7 binary | 16 busy loops | **35/40** | 1885 / 2811 ms | (not instrumented) |
| v2.14.4 + instrumentation | idle | **11/40** | 14 / 3006 ms | 14, including all 11 slow runs |
| v2.14.4 + instrumentation | 16 busy loops | **21/40** | 1237 / 2988 ms | 29, including all 21 slow runs |
| v2.14.4 + instrumentation + fix | idle | 0/40 | 13 / 25 ms | 0 |
| v2.14.4 + instrumentation + fix | 16 busy loops | 0/40 | 26 / 58 ms | 0 |

- Every slow run had `DATA(p)` datagrams discarded during `enable()`, and no run without such drops was slow.
- The number of readers still missing at 0.5 s was never larger than the number of discarded `DATA(p)`. It is usually smaller, because the count also includes harmless drops: the peers' periodic announcements, which are sent to every initial-peer port, and the probe's own `DATA(p)`.
- The fast mode is ~125 ms on the 2.14.7 binary and ~14 ms on v2.14.4, with or without the fix. That difference is unrelated to this issue, and I did not investigate it.

The fix used in the last two rows is the one proposed below. A plain reorder of `RegisterReceiver()` before `mp_builtinProtocols->enable()` gave the same result (0/40 slow both idle and loaded; max 25 ms and 38 ms).

### Fast DDS version/commit

v2.14.4 (346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89) and the `ros-jazzy-fastrtps` 2.14.7 binary. Also reproduced on `master` (3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007) and on the `2.14.x` head (b904a742) with the regression test.

### Platform/Architecture

Other. Please specify in Additional context section.
- Production: Linux, about 24 DDS processes on one host.
- Reproducer: Ubuntu 24.04 amd64, Docker `ros:jazzy-ros-base`.

### Transport layer

UDPv4

### Additional context

#### Original deployment

- About 24 participants on one Linux host. One of them is restarted from time to time.
- Localhost-only discovery through UDP unicast initial peers, configured as in the reproducer. The original deployment also used SHM for user data and a different domain id; neither is needed to reproduce.
- A packet capture showed the remote participants' `DATA(p)` answers arriving 1 to 35 ms after the new participant's first `DATA(p)`. The new participant never processed them.
- The time until a restarted participant had matched all remote readers was either below 1 s or 3 to 5 s.
- Shortening `leaseDuration_announcementperiod` to 0.5 s on all participants did not remove the slow mode there.

#### Suggested fix

Send the first announcement only after the receivers are registered:
- Split `announceParticipantState(true)` + `resetParticipantAnnouncement()` out of `BuiltinProtocols::enable()` into a new `BuiltinProtocols::start_participant_announcement()`.
- Call it at the end of `RTPSParticipantImpl::enable()`, after the `RegisterReceiver()` loop.

```cpp
void RTPSParticipantImpl::enable()
{
    mp_builtinProtocols->enable();                          // PDP::enable() only

    //Start reception
    for (auto& receiver : m_receiverResourcelist)
    {
        receiver.Receiver->RegisterReceiver(receiver.mp_receiver);
    }

    mp_builtinProtocols->start_participant_announcement();  // first DATA(p) + periodic announcements
}
```

I prefer this over simply moving the `RegisterReceiver()` loop before `mp_builtinProtocols->enable()`:
- With the simple reorder, reception would start before `PDP::enable()`.
- A discovery server enables its PDP readers already in `PDPServer::init()` ([PDPServer.cpp:120](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/3b4966787cc897a6287c3a6242b22a1dac874007/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDPServer.cpp#L120)).
- So a server would process `DATA(p)` before `PDP::enable()` has done three things: create the lease events of the pooled proxies, run `pre_enable_actions()` (DDB enable or backup restore), and set `enabled_`.
- With the split, everything up to and including `PDP::enable()` stays as it is, and only the first announcement moves.

https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/pull/6631 implements this on `master`, with a deterministic blackbox regression test.

#### Workaround

None found that closes the window. A shorter announcement period only shortens the slow mode, and it did not remove it in the original deployment.

### XML configuration file

None. The reproducer sets the QoS in code (see `common.hpp` in the gist).

### Relevant log output

Fast DDS logs nothing. Reproducer output (v2.14.4 + instrumentation, idle host): one fast run and three slow ones. In the slow runs the matched count (`c500` … `c5000`) stays flat until the remaining peers announce again.

```text
run  2: RESULT match_ms=14 create_ms=2.7 c500=24 c1000=24 c2000=24 c3000=24 c5000=24 startup_drops=1 spdp_drops=1
run  7: RESULT match_ms=3005 create_ms=2.9 c500=16 c1000=16 c2000=16 c3000=24 c5000=24 startup_drops=63 spdp_drops=31
run 10: RESULT match_ms=2924 create_ms=2.7 c500=8 c1000=8 c2000=8 c3000=24 c5000=24 startup_drops=80 spdp_drops=36
run 30: RESULT match_ms=2955 create_ms=2.7 c500=23 c1000=23 c2000=23 c3000=24 c5000=24 startup_drops=14 spdp_drops=14
```

### Network traffic capture

Not attached. In the original deployment, a capture showed the answers arriving 1 to 35 ms after the first `DATA(p)` and never being processed. The reproducer runs entirely on loopback, and the instrumentation shows the drops more directly than a capture would.

TaggedTasks(allow_overriding_keys=True) lets a newly registered factory replace an existing one by function name, but add() writes the new tags without removing the old tag entries. The tags index therefore retains stale membership and references to the replaced factory, and tagged(old_tag) incorrectly returns the replacement even when it was not registered under old_tag. Overriding with no tags leaves every old tag in tags().

Reproduced on current main with replacement factories that change, remove or share tags. Clearing the overridden name from the old tag index and pruning empty tags makes tagged() and tags() reflect the current factory registrations, while preserving unrelated tasks and their registration order.

new_candidates.body:
### Intro

I'm a student working on ML systems. I ran into this while checking how MJCF parsing reports invalid attribute values.

### My setup

MuJoCo 4.0.1 (PyPI wheel, Python API) and main @ bcc80d5 built from source (C API); macOS 26.6.1, arm64.

### What's happening? What did you expect?

For attributes that take several keywords (sensor `contact` and `rangefinder` `data`, the `input` of `pid`/`dcmotor` actuators, camera `output`), a misspelled or repeated keyword gives:

```
XML Error: invalid keyword: '(null)'
XML Error: duplicate keyword: '(null)'
```

I expected the message to name the keyword, as it does for single-keyword attributes: `<geom type="sphre"/>` gives `invalid keyword: 'sphre'`.

The two `mjXError` calls in `mjXUtil::MapValues` ([xml_util.cc#L1103-L1111](https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/bcc80d5b09277c0e5728544f127204b9f499e1fb/src/xml/xml_util.cc#L1103-L1111)) have a `'%s'` in the format string but pass no argument, so the `%s` reads a missing argument (formally undefined behaviour; it prints `(null)` here). `MapValue` passes the key.

### Steps for reproduction

Run the script below. The model with valid `data` loads; the other three fail with `(null)` in place of the keyword.

### Minimal model for reproduction

```xml
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="g" size="1"/>
  </worldbody>
  <sensor>
    <contact geom1="g" data="found frce"/>
  </sensor>
</mujoco>
```

### Code required for reproduction

```python
import mujoco

print("mujoco", mujoco.__version__)
cases = {
    "valid data":         '<contact geom1="g" data="found force"/>',
    "typo in data":       '<contact geom1="g" data="found frce"/>',
    "duplicate in data":  '<contact geom1="g" data="found found"/>',
    "typo in rangefinder": '<rangefinder site="s" data="dist dst"/>',
}
for name, sensor in cases.items():
    xml = f"""
<mujoco>
  <worldbody>
    <geom name="g" size="1"/>
    <site name="s"/>
  </worldbody>
  <sensor>{sensor}</sensor>
</mujoco>"""
    try:
        mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml)
        print(f"{name}: loaded")
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"{name}: {str(e).splitlines()[0]}")
```

Output:

```
mujoco 4.0.1
valid data: loaded
typo in data: XML Error: invalid keyword: '(null)'
duplicate in data: XML Error: duplicate keyword: '(null)'
typo in rangefinder: XML Error: invalid keyword: '(null)'
```

Main @ bcc80d5 gives the same messages, and also for `<pid joint="j" input="pos velocity"/>` and `<camera output="rgb dpth"/>`. Passing the keyword to both `mjXError` calls fixes it (`invalid keyword: 'frce'`, `duplicate keyword: 'found'`). I have that two-line change with a test in `xml_native_reader_test.cc` and will open a PR.

### Confirmations

- [x] I searched the latest documentation thoroughly before posting.
- [x] I searched previous Issues and Discussions, I am certain this has not been raised before.

This report was drafted with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5); the outputs above are from the runs described.

### Ticket Type

Performance regression

### Description

`add_features` and `split_dataset` discard episode-aligned row groups when `_write_parquet` rewrites a packed shard. Episodes share row groups, so episode-scoped streaming must decode unrelated rows before filtering. For a shard below the default row-group size limit, this means decoding the entire projected shard for each requested episode. Recording, aggregation and annotation already preserve episode boundaries using the shared writer added in #3807.

### Environment

Main at `fe1c54594`; Linux, Python 3.12.14, PyArrow 25.0.1, datasets 4.8.5, NumPy 2.2.6. CPU and local files.

### Reproduction

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import mkdtemp
import numpy as np
import pyarrow.parquet as pq
from lerobot.datasets.lerobot_dataset import LeRobotDataset
from lerobot.datasets.dataset_tools import add_features

root = Path(mkdtemp())  # retained for inspection
feature = {"dtype": "float32", "shape": (1,), "names": None}
source = LeRobotDataset.create(
    "local/source", root=root / "source", fps=10,
    use_videos=False, features={"state": feature},
)
for episode in range(2):
    for frame in range(3):
        source.add_frame({"state": np.array([frame], dtype=np.float32), "task": "move"})
    source.save_episode()
source.finalize()
edited = add_features(
    source, {"extra": (np.arange(6, dtype=np.float32), feature)},
    output_dir=root / "edited", repo_id="local/edited",
)
for dataset in (source, edited):
    path = next((dataset.root / "data").glob("*/*.parquet"))
    print(pq.ParquetFile(path).num_row_groups)
```

Observed: `2`, then `1`. Expected: `2`, then `2`, preserving per-episode reads. The same loss occurs when splitting multiple episodes into one output shard, including embedded images.

### Measurement

For 64 episodes × 256 frames with 32 float32 state values per frame, a complete sequence of projected episode reads materializes 1,048,576 rows instead of 16,384. This is decoded Arrow data, not measured network traffic. Reusing the established episode-aligned writer avoids that amplification; smaller groups can increase file size and write cost.

### Checklist

- [x] Searched matching Issues and PRs, including the earlier #3807 change.
- [x] Reproduced on the current main revision above.
- [ ] Verified in another environment.

AI assisted with investigation and reproduction. No full training benchmark was run.

### Description


**What happens.** While the simulation is stopped, `isaacsim.core.experimental.prims.Articulation` falls back from
the tensor backend to its USD backend (`_check_for_tensor_backend`, `articulation.py` line 4665). The USD path gets
each DOF's drive through `_get_drive_api_and_type`, which calls
`Articulation.ensure_api([dof_prim], UsdPhysics.DriveAPI, drive_type)` (line 4796). `ensure_api` applies the API if
the joint does not have it. So any of these calls adds `PhysicsDriveAPI:angular` (or `:linear`) to the joint, in the
stage's current edit target:
- setters: `set_dof_position_targets`, `set_dof_max_efforts`, `set_dof_gains` (run);
- **getters too**: `get_dof_max_efforts`, `get_dof_gains` (run);
- read in the code, not run (their USD branch calls `_get_drive_api_and_type` too): `get_dof_drive_types`,
  `get_dof_position_targets`, `get_dof_velocity_targets`, `get_dof_drive_model_properties`,
  `get_dof_friction_properties`, `set_dof_velocity_targets`, `set_dof_drive_model_properties`,
  `set_dof_friction_properties`. On Newton, `get_dof_friction_properties` also applies `NewtonJointAPI`
  (line 1015).

No warning is logged: the fallback warning (lines 4676–4683) is reached only when a backend was set explicitly
(`backend_utils.is_backend_set()` is False by default).

With PhysX a zero-gain drive on a passive joint is harmless. With the Newton backend it is not: a joint driven by an
`MjcActuator` (the MuJoCo USD schema; this is what an MJCF asset converted to USD carries) has no UsdPhysics drive.
After the call it has one, and on the next play Newton's importer turns it into a different model:
- a drive with the schema's fallback gains (0, 0) is read as effort mode and the `MjcActuator` is not created at all;
- a drive with gains (after `set_dof_gains`) becomes a position + velocity actuator pair (Isaac Sim imports drives
  with `force_position_velocity_actuation=True`), and the `MjcActuator`'s force range lands on the position half only.

**Repro** (attached [stopped_setter_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34811859/stopped_setter_repro.py), headless, Newton backend; output attached as [output_2_stopped_setter.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34811791/output_2_stopped_setter.txt) ). One revolute joint with no UsdPhysics drive, driven by an `MjcActuator` (kp 100,
kv 10, forceRange ±5 N m). For each call: fresh stage, play, stop, ONE call, play, then target 0 → 1 rad for 0.5 s
with `set_dof_position_targets`.

| call while stopped | `DriveAPI` added | authored | MuJoCo actuators after play | θ after 0.5 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none (stop, play only) | no | – | 1 (range ±5) | 0.9934 rad |
| `get_dof_max_efforts()` | **yes** | nothing | **0** | **0.0000** |
| `get_dof_gains()` | **yes** | nothing | **0** | **0.0000** |
| `set_dof_position_targets(0.0)` | yes | targetPosition 0 | **0** | **0.0000** |
| `set_dof_max_efforts(5.0)` | yes | maxForce 5 | **0** | **0.0000** |
| `set_dof_gains(100, 10)` | yes | stiffness, damping | 2 (position ±5, velocity unlimited) | 0.2495 (speed capped at 5 / 10 rad/s) |

No warning was logged in any case. The edit target was the stage's root layer, so saving the stage would keep the drive
(not tested; the drive was seen in the root layer in memory).

**Expected.**
1. A getter never authors anything. If the joint has no drive, return the schema fallback or NaN, or raise.
2. A setter does not silently add a drive API to a joint that has none. At least a warning; better, skip such DOFs
   or raise.
3. Optional: log the USD fallback once by default, not only when a backend was set explicitly.

A guard in `_get_drive_api_and_type` (use the existing `DriveAPI` if `prim.HasAPI(UsdPhysics.DriveAPI, drive_type)`,
otherwise return None and let the callers skip or warn) would cover all callers.

---

**B. Max effort on an `MjcActuator`-driven joint (Newton tensor backend).** Same scene and script, while playing:

| call | read back | what the drive does |
|---|---|---|
| `get_dof_max_efforts()` | 1e+06 | the actuator is limited to 5 N m |
| `set_dof_max_efforts(2.0)` | 2 | peak torque 2.0 N m (joint clamp `jnt_actfrcrange` set to ±2) |
| `set_dof_max_efforts(20.0)` | 20 | peak torque still 5.0 N m (the actuator's range is unchanged) |

`ArticulationView.get_dof_max_forces` / `set_dof_max_forces` read and write Newton's `joint_effort_limit` only
(`isaacsim.physics.newton/python/impl/tensors/articulation_view.py` lines 1345 and 1372 at v6.2.0), which becomes
MuJoCo's joint clamp. An actuator's own force range is not seen. Expected: report the effective limit (the smaller of
the joint limit and the actuator range), or document that max effort is the joint limit and that an actuator range
applies on top of it.


### Isaac Sim version
